prize_name: Benjamin Franklin Medal in Materials Science and Engineering
funder_origin_name: Private benefactors' endowed medal funds at The Franklin Institute (Elliott Cresson Fund 1848, Boyden Premium Fund 1859, Edward Longstreth Fund 1890, Howard N. Potts Fund 1906, The Franklin Fund 1914, Louis E. Levy Fund 1923, John Price Wetherill Fund 1925, Francis J. Clamer Fund 1943 and others), pooled into the Benjamin Franklin Medals at the 1998 reorganization
funder_current_name: The Morel Family Foundation, through the Benjamin Franklin Medalists' Fund at The Franklin Institute
funding_share_basis: The purse is a USD 10,000 honorarium plus a 14-karat gold medal. The Franklin Institute's 2026 Awards Convocation Book, in its 'Awards Endowments' section, attributes the honoraria to one named fund: 'The Benjamin Franklin Medalists' Fund was established in 2017 by The Morel Family Foundation and provides honoraria for Benjamin Franklin Medalists and NextGen Awardees.' The same section separately thanks the donors of 21 legacy named funds (Elliott Cresson 1848, Boyden 1859, Longstreth 1890, Potts 1906, The Franklin Fund 1914, Levy 1923, Wetherill 1925, Clamer 1943, Michelson 1967, Lax 1997, The Bower Fund 1988 and others) as funds that 'support the Bower Awards and the Benjamin Franklin Medals' generally, i.e. the program, not the honoraria. Applying the >50% test to the money: the cash the winner receives today is post-2017 Morel money, not the nineteenth- and twentieth-century bequests that financed the medals at the 1998 founding of the Benjamin Franklin Medals, so most of today's purse is new money and funder_changed is true. This supersedes the earlier 'same money, new vehicle' reading of the 1998 pooling, which was made before this document was located. Two exclusions: the ceremony sponsors (Bank of America, Presenting Sponsor for the 24th consecutive year in 2026; KPMG and Marsha and Jeffrey Perelman, Awards Week; associate sponsors, patrons and benefactors, among them the Morel Family Foundation as an associate event sponsor) underwrite the Awards Ceremony and Dinner and the Institute's STEM programs, which is operations money; and the programme's 'Laureate Sponsors' are Committee on Science and the Arts members presenting the nomination case, not funders. The only residual uncertainty is the gold medal itself, which the Institute does not attribute to a specific fund and which the legacy endowments plausibly still cover; the cash honorarium, the dominant and unambiguous component of the purse, is 100% Morel-funded.
money_note: USD 10,000 honorarium plus a 14-karat gold medal, the same as every other Benjamin Franklin Medal; since 2017 the honoraria for all Benjamin Franklin Medalists (and NextGen Awardees) have been paid from the Benjamin Franklin Medalists' Fund, established that year by The Morel Family Foundation (Doylestown, Pennsylvania; EIN 47-5521535; the family foundation of Donald E. Morel, Jr., a Franklin Institute chair emeritus), before which the medals were carried by the Institute's pooled legacy benefactor endowments.
status_note: Materials science is not one of the seven standing Benjamin Franklin Medal disciplines (chemistry, civil and mechanical engineering, computer and cognitive science, Earth and environmental science, electrical engineering, life science, physics) fixed at the 1998 consolidation, when the Institute folded 25 separately endowed awards (Franklin Medal, last given 1997; Elliott Cresson Medal; Howard N. Potts Medal) under the Benjamin Franklin Medals umbrella. It has been used only as an occasional ad hoc discipline label, under four different wordings: Materials Science (Merton C. Flemings, 2007), Mechanical Engineering and Materials Science (Subra Suresh, 2013), Materials Science and Engineering (Mildred S. Dresselhaus, 2017) and Materials Engineering (John A. Rogers, 2019). The exact name we use was therefore awarded once, in 2017; no materials-labelled medal has been given since 2019 (the 2026 class again covers only standing disciplines), and our winner list correctly shows 'Not awarded' for 2015-2016, 2018 and 2020-2024.
evidence_quote: The Benjamin Franklin Medalists' Fund was established in 2017 by The Morel Family Foundation and provides honoraria for Benjamin Franklin Medalists and NextGen Awardees.
judgment_reason: The honoraria attribution is explicit in the Institute's own 2026 convocation book, so the current purse funder and funder_changed=true are well evidenced; the judgment flags are narrower. (1) The medal itself, unlike the honorarium, is not attributed to any fund and may still be struck on legacy endowment income, so a coder weighting the gold medal's value rather than the cash could read the purse as mixed. (2) The materials label was first used in 2007, after the 1998 pooling and before the 2017 Morel fund, so origin is coded as the parent program's pooled benefactor endowments; a coder could instead treat The Franklin Institute itself as the origin funder, which would leave funder_changed true either way. (3) awarding_org_type is Society (an 1824 membership institute whose Committee on Science and the Arts selects laureates) rather than Philanthropy, arguable since the body is today mainly a donor-funded science museum.
